then.text: You saw the silver shoes. Most people only hear the hoofbeats. The lake will be talking about you for seven years.
You've walked the circle. Now wait by the shore at night, out past the causeway. Listen for hooves on water.
The Grange Stone Circle, east of the lake. Walk in by the entrance, the way the sun does at midsummer, and pay your respects.

else.text: Do you know the story of Gearóid Iarla? The Earl of Desmond, a poet and a magician. His wife begged to see his magic, and he turned into a goose before her eyes. She screamed, and broke the spell, and he vanished into the lake.
Every seven years he rides out across Lough Gur on a white horse shod with silver. When the shoes are worn thin, he'll come back. I've been coming here thirty years to see the shoes.
Walk the Grange Stone Circle first, then come back to the shore at night. The old places listen to those who visit them properly.

then.text: Back to the lake with you. Nóra will have you up all night.

else.text: In through the entrance passage, that's it, the way the midsummer sun comes in. You can feel it, can't you? Four thousand years of people standing just here.
Off you go to the lake. Respects paid.
A hundred and more stones in a ring, and inside the floor was built up a metre with clay. They found broken pots in it: a feast, or a lot of very clumsy people.

then.text: Out on the dark water there's a sound like hooves on stone. A pale horse comes walking over the lake, and its four shoes shine silver in the moonlight.
The shoes are still bright. Gearóid Iarla will be a while yet.

else.text: A thin mist lies on the lake. Nóra said the silver horse rides at night.
A thin mist hangs over the water. It looks, for a moment, like the shape of a horse. Then it's mist again.
